sources_considered.why: read_page returned HTTP 401. The full authorized republication in Mint was used instead.
read_page returned FULL TEXT of the Wall Street Journal report, including its project reporting and qualifications.
Contemporaneous reproduction of Altman's roadmap; treated as a secondary reproduction, not an official forum announcement.
Reuters independently corroborates the roadmap distinction, but the reproduced statement provides the relevant wording more directly.
Primary launch results provide material evidence of improvements that limits a sweeping failure interpretation.
Contemporaneous review substantiates disappointment while also describing improvements. Marcus's comments quoted in the article are not used as corroboration.

evidence_items.publisher: The Wall Street Journal, republished by Mint
evidence_items.locator: Opening section, paragraph describing two large training runs

receipt.public_excerpt: Each time, new problems arose and the software fell short of the results researchers were hoping for, people close to the project say.

evidence_items.explanation: The report identifies the project as GPT-5/Orion and describes missed expectations and delays. No public internal project records were found, so this conclusion relies on reporting from unnamed people familiar with the effort.

evidence_items.publisher: OpenAI Developer Community user reproducing Sam Altman
evidence_items.locator: First post, reproduction of Sam Altman's February 12 roadmap

receipt.public_excerpt: We will next ship GPT-4.5, the model we called Orion internally, as our last non-chain-of-thought model.

evidence_items.explanation: Connects Orion to GPT-4.5. The surrounding roadmap describes a subsequent integrated GPT-5 system, limiting any inference that GPT-4.5's reception settled that revised project's prospects.

evidence_items.locator: Appendix, introductory paragraph and following model evaluation table

receipt.public_excerpt: Even by purely scaling up unsupervised learning, GPT‑4.5 shows meaningful improvements over previous models like GPT‑4o.

evidence_items.explanation: The published evaluations show improvements over GPT-4o, providing material counterevidence to interpreting failure as no technical progress. They do not disclose whether Orion met its original internal goals.

evidence_items.locator: Review discussion immediately before 'High on vibes, low on reasoning'

receipt.public_excerpt: However, these incremental gains come with significantly higher computational demands and costs.

evidence_items.explanation: The review characterizes gains as incremental and the release as disappointing relative to its costs, supporting the reception clause. It also acknowledges improvements, so it does not establish universal rejection.

unresolved_gaps: Internal success criteria and complete project results are not public.
The evidence does not establish failure of the revised GPT-5 system roadmap.
